page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.8xlarge is a general-purpose, network- and EBS-optimized server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m8gn.8xlarge demonstrates top-tier memory performance, with large-block read bandwidth reaching 412.91 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 198.33 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is also highly competitive, as evidenced by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21484.0 and strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Database operations are highly efficient, with Passmark database benchmarks scoring in the top 10% and Redis SET operations reaching 66.38 million operations per second.

Tradeoffs include average single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside weak prompt processing speeds for large LLM models. The ARM64 architecture lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX and AMX. However, the high memory bandwidth and dedicated core allocation deliver excellent qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense workloads. This server is highly effective for database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
